Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
If the target of a successful Anathema vote is in combat, and
chooses a strike which costs him his last blood, is he burned
immediately upon paying for the strike, or is he only burned
when the combat is over (or immediately after the strike
resolves)?
--
L. Scott Johnson (sjoh...@math.sc.edu) | Backing into a fan, the firefly
http://www.math.sc.edu/~sjohnson | was delighted to no end!
Graphics Specialist and V:tES Rulemonger. |

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) writes:

>If the target of a successful Anathema vote is in combat, and
>chooses a strike which costs him his last blood, is he burned
>immediately upon paying for the strike, or is he only burned
>when the combat is over (or immediately after the strike
>resolves)?

More thoughts:

If the target is at zero blood before combat (and has his hunt
blocked, for example), does Anathema apply (since the target
isn't reduced to zero "due to combat")?

If the target spends his last blood *before* combat (either by
burning blood to block Donal or a Cam. Exemplary, or by spending
X blood for X maneuvers via the Ruins of Villars Abbey), and is
therfore not reduced to zero during combat (but rather, remains at
zero and is possibly sent to torpor or burned), does the opposing
minion get Anathema credit for the reduction?



Messages.Author: Mark Amidon
Messages.Body:
>sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) writes:

>>If the target of a successful Anathema vote is in combat, and
>>chooses a strike which costs him his last blood, is he burned
>>immediately upon paying for the strike, or is he only burned
>>when the combat is over (or immediately after the strike
>>resolves)?

As that's part of my Brujah Potence-Presence deck, it has come up. The way
we've played it is just as written. Yes, this occasionally means that the
Anathema struggles along emptily, and reduces himself (it was Lazarus, that
Tremere bastard) to avoid the 9-pool jackpot to his prey (me), but that was
fine by me. I just let him hunt (instead of bleed me) for a turn, and beat
him up with a Bum's Rush after he was done.

However, if the Anathema pays for a strike, then he gets to make the strike.
In the above case, that meant that I'd have to hit Lazarus for 4 points of
damage during the second round when he tried to Drain Essence with his last
two blood. No problem when I have Growing Fury. (That's not what transpired,
but that's the way we agreed to play it.)

>More thoughts:

>If the target is at zero blood before combat (and has his hunt
>blocked, for example), does Anathema apply (since the target
>isn't reduced to zero "due to combat")?

No. Bummer, eh? Yet another good reason to put Anathema on one of your
predator's vampires, so that nobody else gets a chance to beat him after the
hunt.

>If the target spends his last blood *before* combat (either by
>burning blood to block Donal or a Cam. Exemplary, or by spending
>X blood for X maneuvers via the Ruins of Villars Abbey), and is
>therfore not reduced to zero during combat (but rather, remains at
>zero and is possibly sent to torpor or burned), does the opposing
>minion get Anathema credit for the reduction?

Nope. This is also a good reason to go off and rescue the poor sot from
Torpor.

Mark Amidon,
Nosferatu-in-training,
Rolling in Lazarus's pool
